tone_statements.quote: The YL Lalo syllable template is (C)V(N)T, in which the optional initial is one of 25 consonants, an obligatory vowel (one of 11 vowels or 1 syllabic fricative), an optional nasal final /-ŋ/, and tone (one of 3 or 4, depending on speaker’s age). tone_statements.citation: Yang, Cathryn (2012). Classifying Lalo languages: Subgrouping, phonetic distance, and intelligibility. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 35(2): 113-137.
tone_statements.quote: PLa has three levels of pitch height in non-harsh phonation (*1, high and modal, *2, low and breathy, *3 mid and modal), and two levels with harsh phonation (*H, mid; *L, low). ... Eka, YL and MD descend directly from PLa and do not share in any Greater Lalo innovations. Instead, they show divergent developments that make them decidedly different from any other Lalo language. MD shows a set of rhyme innovations, Eka shows micro-splits in *1, *2, *H, and *L, and YL shows mergers of *1 and *3 to mid and *L and *H to high. ... [Table 4] YL a) *1 > mid/*[-voi]_, > low-rising/elsewhere b) *L, *H > high (loss of harsh phonation)
tone_statements.locator: p. 118-119 (sec. 2 Background, Proto-Lalo tones) and p. 120-121, sec. 4 'Diachronic subgrouping based on shared innovations', Table 4
tone_statements.summary: Tonal (every syllable carries a lexical tone, per the Lalo/Ngwi background). Proto-Lalo five categories: *1 high modal, *2 low breathy, *3 mid modal, *H mid harsh, *L low harsh. Yangliu reflexes: *1 splits by initial voicing (mid after *voiceless, merging with *3; low-rising elsewhere), *H and *L merge to high with loss of harsh phonation, *2 stays low - i.e. a four-way system mid / low-rising /…

tone.says: Four tones for older speakers: low-rising 24, mid 33, low 21, high falling 53; younger speakers merge 24 into 33, leaving three. All modal phonation; almost every syllable carries a lexical tone.

sources.citation: Yang, Cathryn. 2010. Lalo regional varieties: phylogeny, dialectometry, and sociolinguistics. PhD dissertation, La Trobe University, Bundoora. doi:10.26181/21844209.v1 (447 pp.)
sources.note: Sec. 3.7 'YL' pp. 94-96: syllable template (C)V(N)T, 25 initials (Table 3-41), rhymes (3-42), tones 24/33/21/53 older vs 33/21/53 younger (3-43), all modal; sec. 5.3.4 acoustic tone plots. No statement on word stress/accent for YL or Lalo generally. p. 3: Lalo is 'omnisyllabic' (Matisoff 1989), 'almost every syllable is assigned a lexical tone'. Only incidental 'stressed' in the whole thesis is in the CW-QY (Qingyun) sketch: 'Following a stressed syllable, the syllabic nasal loses its syllabicity and merges with the previous syllable'.
